methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector as a public company. The relevant peer universe comprises seven private companies in the same sector, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro. No public comparables exist in this narrow category, limiting the applicability of traditional peer median approaches.

Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable to this valuation. The sector contains only seven private peers total, and filtering by stage, adjacent stage, or valuation tier yielded fewer than three datapoints in any single cohort. Applying an all-sector median would obscure material differences in business model, technology maturity, and commercialization timelines across the Drones & Autonomous landscape. Consequently, no defensible peer-based valuation multiple could be derived from the available comp set.

This analysis reveals a structural limitation in valuing INVZ using comparable company methods. The public equity markets lack direct public peers, while the private market peer set is too thin and heterogeneous to support reliable multiple-based valuation. Alternative approaches—such as precedent transactions, DCF modeling, or venture-stage benchmarking—would be required to triangulate a credible valuation range. The key uncertainty is the absence of narrow, stage-appropriate comparables; investors should seek additional data on recent funding rounds and exit valuations within the autonomous systems ecosystem to supplement this analysis.
